Check out these two posts from Les_paul: post1 and post2 I think the SPAZ type works only if there is nothing important on the left, like a broken key level. Because the break of a key level makes it an FTR/FL. Also the reason for ITs creating stacked S/D is to pick up orders on the way and on return to fake out all classic S/D and S/R traders. Think about it this way, if ITs created those stacked demand/supply bases to fill their orders on the way, this means that on return there is little possibility of unfilled orders still left there. This is especially true for compression PAZs. That's why price needs to break only the last/first demand just before the CPAZ or SPAZ to make it through the entire zone. So if there are still unfilled orders then they are likely there at the tip (entrance of PAZ) and not inside that consumed zone. Perhaps this is exactly what IF means by saying that we need to make that final juxtaposition, where we see those concepts all at the same time. Often there is this common question in the homework section: "Why did that or this FTR/FL/CP/... fail?" Because it was never meant to work that way. Looking at the charts, there are almost dead sure setups that present itself only if multiple of the above RTM concepts appear together in the same setup. For example: at HTF supply, a trick is played (FO) then at the right shoulder of the trick level price forms an FTR/FL which happens to be a QM level also. Price meanwhile broke a lower FL and starts to retrace to the QM level. On approach price is starting to compress (making a CPAZ). Once price hits the QM FTR level at the FO key level at HTF supply price bounces and breaks into the CPAZ. If price now retraces back to the origin for a second chance entry then you have one of those almost dead sure trades Something like this past setup: Jurij wrote: CADJPY 30m Had a limit sell order not triggered, too high https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2410-jurij-s-corner?start=225 15/53 7/27/2018 Jurij's Corner - Page 10 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT 5m LTF second chance (missed this one too) I think those setups are really nice and clear, that's what I want to trade more. I tried only trading in the direction of the HTF scale Engulf but when this is 4 hour or higher the best trades are on a deep retrace of the HTF Engulf at least for R:R. Having said that trading the LTF scale engulf in the opposite direction of the HTF engulf produces good trades. I hope to be able to do this consistently Journal review: Jurij wrote: NZDCAD DM in play? 4H 30m https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2410-jurij-s-corner?start=450 9/58 7/27/2018 Jurij's Corner - Page 19 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT initial QM spotted by a trading mate, so not all my credit Looking back at this, at that time it was a solid looking setup to me. The problem and the error I've been doing is to consider scales, making everything more complicated than it is, especially mixing smaller and higher scale FTR/FL boxes. But the market doesn't care about boxes with fixed rules (for ex. 4H box is stronger than 5m box and an eng is a signal...). If a 4H FTR/FL box is made as a reaction to a 1m FL it is because of these orders sitting there. Orders have not time frames because they are just orders. There are levels that are stronger than others, not because of time frame but because of orders and decisions of greater or lesser importance (swap levels vs simple barriers...) First the charts https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2410-jurij-s-corner?start=25 2/54 7/27/2018 Jurij's Corner - Page 2 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT As you can see price stopped at the first opposing FL of that scale (good for 1st profit tg). Then the pivot low 30m FL base, was not a good point for the full reversal. Reasons: 1. the base was a pivot low, which means a reaction to a previous base, in this case a 30m FTR (which itself is the top of a small CP) 2. the sharp arrival and departure makes this more a stop hunt/fake out than a full reversal, also because most reversals have larger tops with QM/diamond levels 3.this low (where my entry was) and the pivot low can be used by ITs for future tricks (FO), whereas that small 30m FTR looks absolutely not interesting to retail traders 4. the better entry can be seen on chart #2 after the new 1m engulf signal either at the 1m quasimodo level or at the origin of the engulf, with the stop below the ftr base, I started to doubt about the validity of that engulf, but in the end price reached the target FL above. "...But FOF is only present with PA, until then it is just unfilled orders that could bounce price " many thanks all the best Salivan explained nicely FOF in his jorunal. Basically unfilled orders are one thing but FOF is different. For example if we have unfilled orders we can expect only a bounce. If we have PA (signal/intention) then the last set of unfilled orders becomes FOF as there are no orders beyond that FOF level. Without the signal, we have just the last set of unfilled orders but no guarantee that the level holds. If the ITs filled all their orders beyond a certain level, it doesn't make sense to fake out past it, they must hate drawdown too... That last level will have all limit orders of the ITs to make sure it doesn't break. Once tg is hit, those orders are removed. And price is allowed to break that level. That's my understanding of FOF as of now and since I'm new to FOF as well, I'm not really sure about it yet. Hope it helps. Friedrich Nietzsche QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Jurij's Corner #52 ahdat Offline Trader Posts: 102 Thank you received: 125 Hey Jurij, wanted to give my take on what happened to your trade. That was an engulf where price DID move to the next FL, but that's all you can reasonably expect since you were on such a low time frame. I think the mistake was expecting price to KEEP going down on such a low time frame move. Usually I try to only use the M1 to validate a higher time frame move. I marked up your chart looking at it more holistically. 1. You see price engulfed what looks to be a fairly significant FL. And it engulfed it with https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2410-jurij-s-corner?start=50 3/41 7/27/2018 Jurij's Corner - Page 3 - RTM Community a bull candle (2), which would suggest price wants to go up. At this point I would be HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT looking for an area to enter a long trade. 3. Now price did engulf downward, but it was in the context of a larger move. Price was compressing into the bull candle. At the end of the compression, you would expect price to continue going up. Rather than go short here I would read price is just retracing before continuing its move up. 4. And you see the compression ended right at the s/r flip level, and price continued its move up. The s/r flip level and base of the pole are possible areas to look for a long entry, depending on your risk profile. When starting off, try to stick to the higher time frames for analysis. I bet if you were looking at the m5 or m15, it would have been easier to see that price wanted to move up. LOGOUT HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE Just a quick question, how you know which is the retailer stop? You know all retailers who follow trend put their stop below the last newly formed high/low in expectation for a trend continuation (new high/low). So retailer stops are just beyond pivot highs/lows, but here at RTM we know that the true orders are at the FTRs and those highs/lows are made sometimes to build traps so that ITs take the stops from retailers to get some extra liquidity. In that way, even if they are right on the direction, they lose. The idea with that chart is, once you know the new direction and target price wants to follow, when you see some highs or lows just above/below a fresh FTR then it is likely that price fakes out to the fresh zone. I saw the opportunity for a setup by looking on what flag limits/FTRs are important. For me your FTR3 is not important because it did not break anything on the left (on that scale). Price made a range (a box), meaning price flagged between two FTRs. Once price broke out to the upside from that range it made an FTR, a decision that price was to cheap below. Once this FTR breaks, the decision is made that price is no longer cheap and price is free to move to the other FTR which caused price to flag previously in that range (previous decision point that price was too cheap). The stacked demand zone was not involved to see the trade opportunity because at that time the SPAZ wasn't there yet. Only the demand which is a reaction to your FTR3 made it a SPAZ. And there are no clues that price will go https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2410-jurij-s-corner?start=200 21/53 7/27/2018 Jurij's Corner - Page 9 - RTM Community to the other end of the SPAZ until price engulfs the latest demand (tip of PAZ).
